equivalent: In this match arm `mask` is read in exactly one place -- `mask & (1 << k)` inside `for k in 0..width` -- and for a VECT_8 word `width` is 8, so only bits 0..=7 are ever tested. `payload & 0x00FF` equals `payload` on bits 0..=7 by definition of the AND and differs only on bits 8..=11, which the loop never reaches; `width` and the advance of `vect_base` are computed from `code`, not from `mask`, and nothing after the tuple reads `payload` again. So for every 16-bit input word the two expressions give the same loop outcomes and therefore the same events, markers, errors and offsets: no input could tell them apart. The observable decision a test could pin instead is a different one -- refusing a VECT_8 whose unused bits 11-8 are set -- and this review did not locate a statement that those bits are guaranteed zero on the wire, so making the decoder refuse real Prophesee recordings on that guess is a change this module makes only on a source's word (Aedat2Layout::DAVIS346 masks its bit 10 because jAER's DavisChip.java and iniVation's AEDAT 2.0 page both say what that bit is; this review located nothing that says what bits 11-8 of a VECT_8 are). Fixture, built and run for the 2026-09 aer correction: two slim copies of the crate, one unmutated and one with this edit, decode every VECT_8 word (all 4096 payloads) alone, after a row with no base, and after a row and each VECT_BASE_X column 0..=2047 of both polarities followed by a VECT_12 of all ones, comparing the Debug text of the two results: 16,785,408 streams, 0 disagreements. The same fixture against a mutant masking with 0x007F instead reports 8,318,912 disagreements, so it can fail.
